es: Localizar en un relato oído el fondo habitual, el giro, la reacción, la consecuencia y la reflexión, e inferir el sentido de la reflexión final.

vocabulary.es: en las secuelas, tras lo ocurrido
aceptar, hacerse a la idea de

teaching.en: The background shows the habit before anything changes: 'We used to have lunch at my grandmother's every Sunday, and we expected the afternoon to unfold just as it always had.'
teaching.es: El fondo muestra el hábito antes de que cambie algo: «Solíamos comer en casa de mi abuela todos los domingos y esperábamos que la tarde se desarrollara como siempre».
teaching.explanationEs: Background = lo que ocurría antes: suele usar used to, would o pasado continuo; unfold = desarrollarse.
segments: The background shows the habit before anything changes: 'We used to have lunch at my
grandmother's every Sunday, and we expected the afternoon to unfold just as it always had.'
teaching.audioText: The background shows the habit before anything changes: 'We used to have lunch at my grandmother's every Sunday, and we expected the afternoon to unfold just as it always had.'

teaching.en: A twist is a change nobody expects, so the narrator is often caught off guard, and words like 'until' or 'suddenly' usually announce it.
teaching.es: Un giro es un cambio que nadie espera, así que el narrador suele quedar tomado por sorpresa, y palabras como «until» o «suddenly» suelen anunciarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Caught off guard = sorprendido sin tiempo de reaccionar; until y suddenly funcionan como señales.
segments: A twist is a change nobody expects, so the narrator is often
caught off guard, and words like 'until' or 'suddenly' usually announce it.
teaching.audioText: A twist is a change nobody expects, so the narrator is often caught off guard, and words like 'until' or 'suddenly' usually announce it.

teaching.en: The shift usually comes with a signal such as 'until one evening' or 'but then', and the verb tense moves from habit to a single event.
teaching.es: El cambio suele llegar con una señal como «hasta que una noche» o «pero entonces», y el tiempo verbal pasa del hábito a un suceso único.
teaching.explanationEs: Shift es el paso de la rutina al suceso; escucha la señal y el cambio de tiempo verbal.
segments: The shift usually comes with a signal such as 'until one evening' or
'but then', and the verb tense moves from habit to a single event.
teaching.audioText: The shift usually comes with a signal such as 'until one evening' or 'but then', and the verb tense moves from habit to a single event.

teaching.en: The reaction tells us how the character felt: 'I froze, and it took a long time for the news to sink in.'
teaching.es: La reacción nos dice cómo se sintió el personaje: «Me quedé helado y tardé mucho en asimilar la noticia».
teaching.explanationEs: Reaction = lo que siente o hace justo después del giro; sink in = calar, asimilarse.
segments: The reaction tells us how the character felt: 'I froze, and
it took a long time for the news to sink in.'
teaching.audioText: The reaction tells us how the character felt: 'I froze, and it took a long time for the news to sink in.'

teaching.en: The consequence is what changed afterwards, and in the aftermath the characters often have to come to terms with a new reality: 'Since that night, we have eaten at different times.'
teaching.es: La consecuencia es lo que cambió después, y tras lo ocurrido los personajes suelen tener que aceptar una nueva realidad: «Desde aquella noche, hemos cenado a horas distintas».
teaching.explanationEs: Consequence suele ir con since y el presente perfecto; in the aftermath = después de un suceso importante.
segments: The consequence is what changed afterwards, and in the aftermath the characters often have to come
to terms with a new reality: 'Since that night, we have eaten at different times.'
teaching.audioText: The consequence is what changed afterwards, and in the aftermath the characters often have to come to terms with a new reality: 'Since that night, we have eaten at different times.'

teaching.en: The reflection closes the story with meaning: 'Looking back, I realise that, slowly, everything began to fall into place.'
teaching.es: La reflexión cierra la historia con sentido: «Mirando atrás, me doy cuenta de que, poco a poco, todo empezó a encajar».
teaching.explanationEs: Reflection es la idea final; «looking back» es su señal más frecuente; fall into place = encajar.
segments: The reflection closes the story with meaning: 'Looking back, I
realise that, slowly, everything began to fall into place.'
teaching.audioText: The reflection closes the story with meaning: 'Looking back, I realise that, slowly, everything began to fall into place.'

prompt.es: Elige la señal que anuncia el giro de la historia.

choices.text: every night
nobody ever checked
until one evening

feedback.es: «Until one evening» rompe la rutina y anuncia el cambio; las otras dos expresiones pertenecen al fondo habitual.

hint.es: Busca la expresión que rompe la rutina.

origin.text: We used to eat dinner together every night, and nobody ever checked a phone, until one evening a call from the hospital changed the mood of the whole house.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tardé una semana entera en asimilar la noticia.»

feedback.es: Sink in describe lo que pasa cuando una noticia por fin se asimila; es típico de la pieza de la reacción.

hint.es: Es el verbo de algo que «cala» poco a poco.

origin.text: At first I simply kept repeating that it could not be true. It took me a whole week for the news to ___ in.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mirando atrás, todo empezó a encajar.»

answer.text: Looking back everything began to fall into place

feedback.es: La reflexión se abre con «Looking back» y usa «fall into place» para el sentido final.

hint.es: Empieza con la señal de la reflexión.

prompt.es: Escucha la anécdota y elige cuál fue la consecuencia del giro.

choices.text: The family drifted apart for a while after the sale.
The narrator stayed angry and refused to forgive him.
The uncle moved to a flat closer to the farm.

feedback.es: La consecuencia llega tras «In the aftermath»: la familia se distanció; la rabia es la reacción y la comprensión final es la reflexión.

origin.audio: We used to spend every Saturday at my uncle's farm, and I never imagined that anything there could change. Until the day he sold it without telling anyone. I was caught off guard, and I stayed angry for months. In the aftermath, we drifted apart, but last spring I went to see him in the little flat he had moved to. Looking back, I understand that the farm was simply too big for a man of seventy.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase de esta historia con la pieza que representa.

pairs: Every evening my father would read to us by the fire.
Then, without warning, the lights went out for good.
I sat there in silence, and I could not take it in.
Since that night, we have lived without a television.
Looking back, those winter nights were the best.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple una función: hábito anterior, suceso inesperado, emoción, efecto duradero y balance final.

pairs: Every evening my father would read to us by the fire.
Then, without warning, the lights went out for good.
I sat there in silence, and I could not take it in.
Since that night, we have lived without a television.
Looking back, those winter nights were the best.

prompt.es: Decide qué pieza de la anécdota es este fragmento.

choices.text: The background before the change
The reaction to the twist
The final reflection

feedback.es: Describe lo que siente y hace el narrador justo después de recibir la noticia: es la reacción, no el hábito previo ni el balance final.

origin.text: My hands went cold, and for a long moment I could not hear anything around me. I just sat there, staring at the table, while everybody else carried on talking about lunch.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sentido da la narradora a su reflexión final.

choices.text: What she dreaded most was the size of the audience itself.
What she feared was being blamed afterwards by her boss.
What she really feared was getting things wrong in public.

feedback.es: La reflexión separa el miedo al público del miedo a equivocarse delante de la gente: lo que temía era el error visible, no a las personas.

origin.audio: I used to be terrified of speaking in public. Then, out of the blue, my boss asked me to present our results to two hundred people. My legs were trembling, but I spoke. Afterwards, several colleagues came to thank me, and the following month I was offered a new role. Looking back, I see that the fear was never really about the audience. It was about making mistakes in front of people.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige por qué menciona que varios colegas fueron a darle las gracias.

choices.text: To show the positive consequences of the twist.
To show how she felt about the twist.
To reflect on what the fear was really about.

feedback.es: Los agradecimientos y el nuevo puesto son lo que cambió después del giro: forman la consecuencia de la anécdota.

origin.audio: I used to be terrified of speaking in public. Then, out of the blue, my boss asked me to present our results to two hundred people. My legs were trembling, but I spoke. Afterwards, several colleagues came to thank me, and the following month I was offered a new role. Looking back, I see that the fear was never really about the audience. It was about making mistakes in front of people.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tras meses de planes, el arrendador canceló y me tomó por sorpresa.»

feedback.es: Caught off guard describe a quien se ve sorprendido sin tiempo de reaccionar, como el narrador ante el giro que rompe sus planes.

origin.text: We had planned every detail of the move for months. Then the landlord called and cancelled the contract, and I was completely caught off ___.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Después, tuvo que aceptar lo ocurrido.»

answer.text: In the aftermath she had to come to terms with it

feedback.es: «In the aftermath» sitúa la consecuencia y «come to terms with» expresa la aceptación.

prompt.es: Lee la reflexión y elige qué actitud muestra la narradora hacia el revés.

choices.text: She still blames the client for ending the contract with them.
She now sees it as painful but in the end useful.
She regrets not having looked for customers abroad earlier.

feedback.es: Dice que fue lo peor, pero reconoce que la obligó a buscar clientes fuera y así sobrevivieron: ve el revés como doloroso y a la larga útil.

origin.text: I used to think that losing the contract was the worst thing that could happen to a small company like ours. We were caught off guard, and for weeks the office felt very sad. But, looking back, it forced us to look for customers abroad, and that is how we saved the business.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué revela la conducta del narrador.

choices.text: Anger directed at the person who had given him the bad news.
Relief that the long wait was finally over.
Shock so deep that he could not speak or think clearly.

feedback.es: Soltar la taza, huir sin hablar y conducir en silencio muestran una reacción de shock profundo, no de enojo ni de alivio.

origin.audio: I dropped my cup, ran to the car without a word and drove for an hour with the radio off, not able to believe what I had heard.

prompt.es: Completa: «Años después, mirando atrás, todo empezó a encajar.»

feedback.es: Fall into place describe cómo las piezas de una historia encajan con el tiempo, típico de la reflexión final.

origin.text: Nothing made sense at the time. But years later, looking back, everything began to ___ into place, and I understood why she had made that decision.
